synthesis.dominant_design_lesson: The product, anchored to an immutable regulatory identifier, must be the atomic unit; the company must be a resolved attribution over that anchor rather than the primary key. Products have hard keys (registration certificate number, 510(k) number, FDA product code) and are therefore tractable; companies have only names and are where all seven platforms are weakest. NextDevice, DevicePro, Joinchain and MedVantage all anchor on a regulatory key; CMOP (company/ticker anchored) and Clarivate (analyst-segment anchored) cannot express product generations, product matching, or reproducible share.
synthesis.second_lesson: Publish the normalisation rules and the taxonomy. NextDevice writes down its de-duplication rules (same batch / same party / same product, across single-platform multiple publication, multi-platform republication, and differing provincial numbering) - the most reusable artefact in the audit. The rules are free; execution is the moat.
industry_consensus_model: Company (role-typed: manufacturer / registrant / agent / filer / buyer)
Classification (regulator-inherited: FDA product code, CN class I/II/III)
Market track / sector (commercial, up to 4 levels)
Tender line (brand, model, price, volume, buyer)
open_lanes: published validation for any predictive claim (0 of 7)
per-record as-of dating and point-in-time versioning (0 of 7)
company resolution methodology with merge audit trail and confidence (0 of 7)
technology generation semantics - field named by 1 of 7, defined by none
inspectable schema or public sample records (0 of 7)
machine-readable public web presence (Joinchain fails completely, Clarivate 403s non-browser clients)
published terms and data licence (GBI publishes none, Clarivate/NextDevice/DevicePro none publicly)
marketing_claims_without_evidence: Clarivate: forecast pipeline movements, financial models and timelines accurately - no metric, no backtest, no methodology
Clarivate: predict granular device pipeline shifts - product adjective, not capability
GBI: AI-driven data governance and correlation analysis - no mechanism, no evaluation
GBI: traceable / 可追溯 - no citation field exhibited publicly
CMOP: finds subsidiaries, brand names and products automatically - no ER mechanism; documented mechanism is hash dedup
CMOP: returns cited, accurate intelligence, not hallucinations - no eval set, no error rate
CMOP: 99.9% uptime, SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA Ready, 200+ teams - no certificate, auditor, or status page cited
MedVantage: applicant, owner-operator and brand names reconciled into a single company - no accuracy, no merge log, no correction path, pre-launch
NextDevice: global device tag system connected - no node list or crosswalk published
DevicePro: 12W+ products and 285W+ products, 7.8万 and 11W+ companies on the same page - self-contradicted
Joinchain: 国内首个 (first in China) claimed three times - self-attributed priority, no independent source
NextDevice / DevicePro / Joinchain: AI + human quality warranty - no inter-annotator agreement, precision, recall, or error rate
synthesis.positive_control: MedVantage makes no prediction claim and labels its own mock UI as illustrative - the only platform whose public claims are calibrated to what it has actually built.
synthesis.confidence_ceiling: All seven are closed; no internal schema, record count, algorithm behaviour, or measured data quality is observable. Every data-structure section is a reconstruction from marketing copy or self-published announcements. Joinchain evidence is materially weaker than the rest (primary site unreadable; taxonomy facts statement-level only). No platform documents Chinese/English name-pair handling, so that specific MedRadar pain point has zero industry evidence in this corpus.
